papers.title: Major Ebola outbreak is escalating: what happens next
papers.body_text: You have full access to this article via your institution. Download the Nature Podcast 22 May 2026 On 17 May the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an ongoing Ebola outbreak a public health emergency of international concern. Centred on the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, the outbreak has seen mounting numbers of suspected cases and deaths linked to the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola virus. In this podcast we hear what's currently known about the outbreak and the efforts of clinicians, researchers and public health officials to halt its progress. Nature: Ebola outbreak is a global health emergency: what happens next Nature: Race begins to trial Ebola drugs amid current outbreak Nature: Ebola outbreak spirals out of control: how might it have started? Nature: Will this Ebola outbreak be the biggest yet? Subscribe to Nature Briefing, an unmissable daily round-up of science news, opinion and analysis free in your inbox every weekday. Never miss an episode. Subscribe to the Nature Podcast on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube Music or your favourite podcast app. An RSS feed for the Nature Podcast is available too.

papers.title: India’s diplomats are hosting the world
papers.body_text: India’s diplomats are hosting the world Asia | Busy doing nothing India’s diplomats are hosting the world But what is getting done? May 21st 2026 India’s determination to stay on good terms with all major powers often proves awkward. A traffic jam of meetings in Delhi this month is making its acrobatics look especially complex. On May 14th India welcomed foreign ministers from the BRICS—a bloc of 11 countries including China and Russia who like to complain about Western hegemony. On May 26th it will host foreign ministers from America, Australia and Japan—who with India make up the “Quad” of countries seeking to check China’s rise. “May is a live minefield for India,” says Constantino Xavier at the Centre for Social and Economic Progress, a think-tank in Delhi. The BRICS meeting was overshadowed by the war in the Gulf. These days the grouping includes both Iran and the United Arab Emirates, whose armed forces have been exchanging blows. So it is no great surprise that the talks concluded without a joint statement. For India this was probably a relief; it would not have approved language that condemned America for the violence. It much prefers BRICS to focus on things no one can dislike. One of its priorities as its chair in 2026 is to promote a “mission for healthy lifestyles”. If core members of BRICS find India disappointingly cautious, the country has sometimes also been seen as a nervy partner for the Quad. Now that bloc is on life-support, in large part because Donald Trump, who is chasing Chinese business deals, appears to have lost interest in it. The other member countries, for their part, have lost trust in Mr Trump. Foreign diplomats in Delhi think the Quad could yet achieve some modest advances in security. These would include building interoperable naval and communications systems, and working to break China’s stranglehold on critical minerals and emerging technologies. But no one expects breakthroughs at the meeting in Delhi this month. The best result of the foreign ministers’ talks might be to approve plans for another meeting. India hopes a gaffe-free gathering will persuade Mr Trump to come to its capital for a summit of Quad leaders later this year. Such a visit was supposed to have taken place in 2025, but was called off when Mr Trump began hiking tariffs on Indian exports. Some in the foreign ministry and prime minister’s office have begun asking if India has signed up to too many initiatives and coalitions, inflating expectations of its capacity and courage. These days “there is less domestic benefit in playing global host,” thinks Dan Markey, an expert on China and South Asia at the Stimson Centre, a think-tank in Washington. Leaders of big powers are giving up the pretence of consulting large groups of the sort India likes to chair. While India was hosting the BRICS ministers, Mr Trump and Xi Jinping were meeting one-on-one in Beijing. Others think India should become much more forthright about the big issues of the day. “We should be able to say to both America and Iran: ‘You cannot hold the world hostage like this’,” says Shivshankar Menon, a former Indian national security adviser and foreign secretary. For years the country’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, sold India as a vishwaguru, or teacher to the world. Yet India very often seems reluctant to divulge what, precisely, it wants the world to learn. ■ Stay on top of our India coverage by signing up to Essential India , our free weekly newsletter. This article was downloaded by zlibrary from https://www.economist.com//asia/2026/05/21/indias-diplomats-are-hosting-the-world

questions.stem: The author uses the metaphor of a 'live minefield' to suggest that India's diplomatic position is ________.

options.B: precarious due to the conflicting demands of its partners
options.C: intentionally disruptive to international power structures
options.D: likely to lead to immediate global geopolitical tension

questions.explanation: 文章提到“May is a live minefield for India”，结合上下文，印度在五月同时主持BRICS（包括俄罗斯和伊朗）和Quad（旨在制衡中国的联盟），这种左右逢源的姿态使其处于极其微妙且容易出错的境地，故选B。

questions.stem: Why does the author suggest that the lack of a joint statement at the BRICS meeting was a 'relief' for India?

options.A: It allowed India to avoid publicly opposing the United States.
options.B: It signaled that the BRICS bloc is becoming irrelevant.
options.C: It prevented further conflict between Iran and the UAE.
options.D: It enabled India to shift the focus toward its own domestic priorities.

questions.explanation: 文中明确指出“it would not have approved language that condemned America for the violence”，因此如果不发表联合声明，印度就可以避免被卷入谴责美国的立场中，这对其外交平衡有利。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the current state of the 'Quad' is best described as ________.

options.A: a robust security alliance gaining momentum
options.B: a platform for immediate economic breakthroughs
options.C: a weakening partnership struggling with inconsistent leadership
options.D: a strictly ceremonial group with no concrete security goals

questions.explanation: 文章提到Quad“on life-support”，部分原因是特朗普对该机制失去兴趣，且成员国之间失去了信任，这反映了该机制目前处于脆弱且低效的状态。

questions.stem: What is the main concern of some officials within the Indian government regarding the country's diplomatic strategy?

options.A: India is neglecting its regional responsibilities in South Asia.
options.B: The country lacks the financial resources to host so many summits.
options.C: India is overcommitting itself and setting unrealistic expectations.
options.D: The diplomatic initiatives are failing to attract Western investment.

questions.explanation: 文中提到官员们开始怀疑印度是否加入了过多的倡议和联盟，从而“inflating expectations of its capacity and courage”，即担优过度承诺导致能力与外界期待不符。

questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the author's critique of India's role as 'vishwaguru'?

options.A: India's leadership is too dogmatic and forceful.
options.B: India talks about teaching the world but lacks a clear vision.
options.C: India’s focus on global issues is at the expense of its own economy.
options.D: India has failed to secure a leadership position in international think-tanks.

questions.explanation: 作者指出尽管莫迪将印度定位为“vishwaguru”（世界导师），但“India very often seems reluctant to divulge what, precisely, it wants the world to learn”，暗示其缺乏明确的核心价值观或教学内容。

papers.title: Debt
papers.body_text: Debt Poems Debt By Daniel Poppick September 20, 2026 What debt is this whose currency is sleep? What clued me in To your delay? What’s the content of a leaf? Who’s fool enough To commune in them? What choice poisons Commingle with chlorophyll To chase us to the other end Of decay? To what address can we send the flowers Or in lieu of flowers What fund should we invest with this thousand-mile Stare through flaming Fields of aster, star-torched tendrils of our Vision insisting In pale ashy patterns to leave some room For the ghost’s donation? Can I ask who’s calling? Aren’t you Sleeping in? When will I wake, erased by a glacial gaze Frozen out Like a convex plinth of air’s obsession With a pyramid? What’s a poem compared to a mouth? Who’s there to hear it? Why are all your texts written in Invisible ink At this late hour? To whom Do I owe the pleasure? This is drawn from “Lines and Circles.”

questions.stem: In the opening lines, what does the poet suggest about the nature of 'debt'?

options.A: It is a financial obligation requiring monetary repayment.
options.B: It is a metaphor for a personal or psychological toll that costs one their rest.
options.C: It represents an actual exchange of currency for sleep-inducing items.
options.D: It is a literal calculation of time lost due to insomnia.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'debt is this whose currency is sleep' metaphorically equates the 'debt' to the loss of sleep, implying it is an abstract or emotional burden rather than a literal financial one.

questions.stem: What does the 'thousand-mile stare' in the middle of the poem likely symbolize?

options.A: The poet's desire to travel long distances to find a cure.
options.B: A state of dissociation, detachment, or intense contemplation of mortality.
options.C: The physical distance between the poet and the recipient of the poem.
options.D: A clear, focused vision of the future.

questions.explanation: The 'thousand-mile stare' is an idiomatic expression for a blank, vacant gaze often associated with trauma, exhaustion, or being lost in deep, detached thought, fitting the poem's melancholic and existential tone.

questions.stem: What does the question 'What’s a poem compared to a mouth?' imply?

options.A: Poetry is superior to verbal communication.
options.B: The poet finds writing poems more difficult than speaking.
options.C: Poetry may be inadequate or hollow compared to direct, physical human existence.
options.D: The 'mouth' represents the source of the poems.

questions.explanation: The contrast between the written poem and the 'mouth' (symbolizing breath, voice, life, and physical consumption) suggests the poet questions the efficacy or validity of art when faced with the raw reality of life and decay.

questions.stem: Why are the 'texts' in the poem described as being written in 'invisible ink'?

options.A: Because they were written by a spy.
options.B: To emphasize that the message is intended for a specific recipient.
options.C: To convey a sense of obscurity, lack of transparency, or the elusiveness of communication.
options.D: Because the paper is of a high-quality, translucent material.

questions.explanation: The 'invisible ink' metaphor reinforces the poem’s theme of fragmentation and the difficulty of communicating meaningful content in a state of confusion or late-night existential dread.

questions.stem: What is the overall tone and thematic focus of this poem?

options.A: A celebratory tribute to the creative process of writing poetry.
options.B: An analytical study of environmental degradation and nature.
options.C: An inquiry into the nature of memory, loss, and the boundaries of human expression.
options.D: A lighthearted reflection on the nature of interpersonal relationships.

questions.explanation: The poem utilizes complex, abstract imagery (ghosts, glacial gaze, decay, invisible ink) to explore existential questions about mortality, the cost of living ('debt'), and the struggle to communicate one's existence.

papers.title: Would-be suicide bomber sets off explosion in NYC
papers.body_text: Police officers stand guard outside the New York Port Authority Bus Terminal in New York City, US December 11, 2017 after reports of an explosion. [Photo/Agencies] A would-be suicide bomber set off part of a homemade explosive device in a subway passage between Times Square and the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown Manhattan during Monday's morning rush hour, seriously wounding himself and injuring three others, police said. The injuries to two commuters and a Port Authority police officer were all non-life threatening, according to the New York Fire Department. At a news conference, Mayor Bill de Blasio called the blast an attempted terrorist attack, and he said no other devices had been found. The suspect was identified by police as Akayed Ullah, 27, a Bangladeshi native, who lived in Brooklyn. He was in serious condition at Bellevue Hospital Center. Ullah acted alone, police said, and the device was reported to have gone off prematurely in the passage just 200 feet from the bus terminal at West 42nd Street and Eighth Avenue — one of the busiest transit hubs in the country — at 7:20 am, authorities said. Two commuters and a Port Authority police officer suffered minor injuries, officials said. The device was affixed to Ullah's body with Velcro and zip ties, police officials said. The explosion caused commuter chaos at one of the city's key traffic hubs. "Our lives revolve around the subway," the mayor said. "The choice of New York is always for a reason, because we are beacons of the world. And we show that a society of many background and many faiths can work." "The terrorists want to undermine that," he added. "They yearn to attack New York City." "I'm glad I wasn't there. We were supposed to take a bus out at the time (when the accident happened), so I'm glad we waited," said Monica Gannon, who planned to take the bus back to New Jersey at this morning when the explosion happened. "We are stuck here. Now we are waiting for all this to be over and go back home." "I was evacuated from the terminal after it (the explosion) happened. It was terrible, and I was so scared when I saw some people running,"said Alicia Carmona. She said she was evacuated from the terminal after the explosion and to wait outside the bus terminal for about two hours. Carmona said she planned to pick up her niece at LaGuardia Airport at around 9 am, but now she couldn't make it. "I was thinking to take the subway instead, but the nearby subway stations are closed too."

questions.stem: According to the passage, what can be inferred about the impact of the explosion on the commuters?

options.A: It caused widespread fatalities among the travelers at the terminal.
options.B: The majority of the injured victims were in critical condition.
options.C: The explosion resulted in significant operational disruptions at a major transit hub.
options.D: Commuters were largely unaffected as the incident occurred away from the main terminal.

questions.explanation: 文章提到爆炸发生在繁忙的交通枢纽附近（one of the busiest transit hubs in the country），导致通勤混乱（commuter chaos），且文中有多处关于撤离（evacuated）和车站关闭（stations are closed）的描述，证实了运营受到严重干扰。A项与原文中injury non-life threatening不符，B项原文说是minor injuries，D项与事实不符。

questions.stem: Why does Mayor Bill de Blasio suggest that terrorists target New York City?

options.A: Because the city lacks sufficient security measures for its subways.
options.B: Because the city represents the values of diversity and coexistence they aim to challenge.
options.C: Because the city's geographical layout makes it an easy target for homemade devices.
options.D: Because the city is the center of global political instability.

questions.explanation: 市长提到New York is a beacon of the world，象征着多种族和多信仰社会的成功融合，而恐怖分子想要undermine（破坏）这一点。因此B选项准确概括了市长对于恐怖分子动机的判断。

questions.stem: The phrase 'would-be suicide bomber' implies that the suspect:

options.A: Attempted to kill himself but failed to succeed.
options.B: Was apprehended before he could set off the device.
options.C: Acted in collaboration with a larger terrorist cell.
options.D: Was planning to surrender after causing the explosion.

questions.explanation: 文章指出嫌疑人虽然引爆了装置并严重受伤（seriously wounding himself），但他还活着并在医院接受治疗，且并未成功实施预期中的大规模自杀式袭击。'would-be'在这里指其意图成为自杀式炸弹袭击者，但结果未遂。

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the nature of the explosive device used by Akayed Ullah?

options.A: It was a military-grade weapon smuggled into the terminal.
options.B: It was a sophisticated mechanism operated by remote control.
options.C: It was a rudimentary device attached to the suspect's person.
options.D: It was a large-scale explosive designed to destroy the entire station.

questions.explanation: 文中明确描述该装置为homemade explosive device（自制爆炸装置），并且是affixed to Ullah's body with Velcro and zip ties（用魔术贴和扎带固定在身体上），符合rudimentary（简陋的）特征。

questions.stem: What is the main concern of the commuters like Monica Gannon and Alicia Carmona?

options.A: The political implications of the terrorist attack.
options.B: The immediate logistical difficulties caused by the evacuation and transit shutdown.
options.C: The long-term safety of the subway system in New York City.
options.D: The lack of medical support for those injured in the explosion.

questions.explanation: Monica Gannon担心的是错过了原定的行程，被困在车站无法回家；Alicia Carmona担心的是无法去机场接侄女，且由于地铁关闭无法寻找替代交通方案。因此，她们的关注点在于当下的交通不便和行程受阻。
